title: No good after 2 years
text: No good after 2 years. We're on our second one. Both have started pocking after a couple years of use. We use it many times per week for poultry, pork, and veggies. The second one, we bought on Amazon, had the supreme  (extra $) long life 25 year coating. Disappointed. Low quality is the world consumers live in now. Won't be buying Joyce Chen again.

product_metadata.title: Joyce Chen 22-0030, Pro Chef Peking Pan with Excalibur Non-stick coating, 12-Inch
features: Versatile carbon steel pan sears satisfying stir fry, but also great for veggies and eggs
Premium Excalibur nonstick coating resists scratching—even with metal utensils
2.0mm professional carbon steel gauge is lighter and stronger than cast iron; heats evenly with no hot spots
Flat bottom and sloped sides are ideal for searing and sautéing
Resin handle stays cool and remains oven safe up to 350 degrees
Without removable handle, pan lets food simmer up to 500 degrees
description: Cook like a pro with this versatile stir-fry pan. A smaller, shallower version of the flat-bottom carbon steel wok, this pan can be used for so many dishes beyond stir-fry—from sauteed veggies to scrambled eggs. Made from carbon steel, it’s lighter and smoother than cast iron, yet just as hardy, with a nonstick coating tough even to withstand the scrapes and rakes of metal utensils. When you pop off the removable resin handle, this pan can also go from stovetop to oven to keep dishes simmering up to 500 degrees.
